sections.html:
Addison is a DuPage County village where most sales involve a suburban house or condo that has to clear a short list of village steps before the deed can move. The July 1, 2025 population estimate is 35,758, a hair above the 35,702 recorded in 2020, so the housing stock is stable and fully built out.

Most houses date from after 1960, when farmland became subdivisions and the population jumped from 6,741 in 1960 to 24,482 in 1970. Owners value their homes at a typical $341,300, and 67.0% of homes are owner-occupied. Typical gross rent is $1,245. Expect buyers of these postwar houses to ask about roofs, furnaces and basements.

sections.h2: Village steps before an Addison sale can close
sections.html:
Addison will not issue a real estate transfer stamp until the sewer, permit, water and paperwork items on the Community Development and Finance pages are cleared. The deed cannot be transferred before the stamp is issued, so a missed item can push back the closing date.

  • Sewer compliance: the certificate cannot be older than six months on closing day, and the village wants the inspection booked two weeks early through Community Development at (630) 693-7530.
  • Permit release: confirms there are no open building permits or unpaid inspection fees. A release stays valid for two months only.
  • Water: the seller books a final meter reading 24 hours before closing and pays the final bill by noon the business day before closing. The buyer pre-registers for the water and sewer account.
  • Paperwork: the seller's attorney sends the village a copy of the PTAX-203 or PTAX-203A and a copy of the drafted deed.

Condominiums skip the water account and the sewer or sump inspection. A condo needs only the permit release.

Addison transfer stamp amounts on the village real estate transfers page
Stamp typeAmountWho pays
Standard transfer stamp$2.50 for each $1,000 of purchase priceBuyer
Exempt transfer stamp (quitclaim, trust, foreclosure, sheriff sale)$50 administrative feeParty requesting the stamp
Transfer of beneficial interest$1.25 per $500 block, rounded upParty transferring

Separately, Section 31-10 of the Property Tax Code puts a state tax of 50 cents on every $500 block of value stated on the transfer declaration. When the deed says the property passes subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage balance is left out of the basis. File the declaration on Form PTAX-203 or through the Department of Revenue's free MyDec system, and have the seller's attorney send the village its own copy at the water billing email on the village page.

The village issues a zero-dollar exempt stamp for quitclaim deeds, deeds into a trust, foreclosures and sheriff sales, and it still charges the $50 processing fee. A lost stamp has to be repurchased in full, so keep the original in the closing file.

The exempt stamp needs the same sewer inspection, permit release and final water bill as a sale. The village also asks for its own Certificate of Exemption form and a copy of the signed and notarized deed. When the owner name on the deed is changing, the new owner opens a water and sewer account with two forms of identification. When the name is not changing, the water balance simply has to be paid before the stamp is released.

Heirs deeding an inherited Addison house should plan on the same items, even though no sale tax is due. Starting the sewer appointment early is the best way to protect the closing date.

sections.h2: Rules for an Addison house that is rented out
sections.html:
Every Addison dwelling that is not owner-occupied and charges rent needs an annual Residential Rental License. The license year runs May 1 to April 30, renewal notices arrive by mail in March, and renewals are due by April 30.

The village counts more than 1,000 rental properties and nearly 4,000 rental units, and it grades each property after an annual inspection. In a single-family house, condo or townhouse the inspector walks the interior. In a multi-family building the village inspects 20 percent of the units plus the common areas. Owners must also attend an 8-hour Crime Free Multi-Housing class within 90 days of getting a license.

Addison bans short-term rentals outright and classes them as a nuisance, so a buyer hoping to use a booking site is out of luck. A landlord selling a rental can email Rentals@addison-il.org or call the Rental Housing Supervisor line at (630) 693-7544 to ask how an open license year is handled at closing.

DuPage County sends one bill with two installment coupons, and the tax covers the prior year. For 2025 taxes, bills went out on April 29, 2026, with payments due on the first of June and the first of September. The DuPage County Treasurer at 630-407-5900 can confirm the dates for the next cycle.

Addison spans Addison and Bloomingdale townships, so the township assessor named on the bill is the first contact for valuation questions. The treasurer's office does not set values. A yellow box on the bill means a mortgage servicer is already paying, and a second payment would later have to be refunded.

  • The general homestead exemption and the senior exemption are each $8,000.
  • Preliminary county figures for the 2025 levy showed assessed value up 8.2%, the average tax rate down 4.37% and the overall bill up 3.83%.
  • Individual bills differ by parcel because each one falls in a different mix of school, park and fire districts.

Because the bill arrives a year behind, ask the title officer how the current year's tax and any unpaid installment will be split between buyer and seller.

sections.h2: Appealing an assessment before you list
sections.html:
An owner can file with the DuPage County Board of Review, but only inside the 30-day window that opens when the township roll is published. Section 16-55 of the Property Tax Code sets the deadline at 30 calendar days after publication, and talking with the township assessor does not extend it.

The county asks for three or more comparable properties, with recent sales as the strongest evidence. Assessed values rest on the three prior years of sales, so the 2025 value drew on sales from 2022 through 2024. Written decisions usually arrive the following March. An owner who disagrees can go on to the state Property Tax Appeal Board or to court. An appeal challenges the assessed value only, and the tax rate stays with the local taxing districts.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits an Addison house?
sections.html:
Addison owners can hire an agent, sell on their own, or sell to a buyer who accepts the house in its current condition. A cash buyer still needs the same sewer certificate, permit release and final water bill, so the village timetable applies on every route. Inherited, tenant-occupied or heavily worn houses often go the as-is route because repairs would otherwise be negotiated after the buyer's inspection.

Whichever way you go, call Community Development first, ask what is open on your address and book the sewer inspection. Then line up the water readings and have your attorney prepare the declaration and deed copies so the stamp can be released on time.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I book the Addison sewer inspection?
faqs.a: Call Community Development at (630) 693-7530 and set the appointment at least two weeks ahead. The certificate must be dated within six months of closing.

faqs.q: Who pays the Addison real estate transfer stamp?
faqs.a: The buyer. The standard rate is $2.50 for each $1,000 of purchase price.

faqs.q: Do condos in Addison need a sewer inspection?
faqs.a: No. Condos skip the water and sewer account and the sewer and sump pump inspection. A permit release is the only requirement.

faqs.q: Can a buyer run an Addison house as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: No. Addison prohibits short-term rentals and treats them as a nuisance. Long-term rentals need the annual Residential Rental License and an inspection.

faqs.q: What were the DuPage County property tax installment dates?
faqs.a: The 2025 taxes came due on the first of June and the first of September 2026. The DuPage County Treasurer can confirm the next dates, and you should check whether a mortgage servicer already pays your taxes before sending money.
